entries.author: William Shakespeare
entries.original:
Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Sonnet 18
entries.reading:
Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
entries.explanation: The poem begins with a comparison to summer, then asks how words can preserve beauty beyond a season.

entries.author: Emily Dickinson
entries.original:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Hope
entries.reading:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
entries.explanation: Hope becomes a small singing bird. The image suggests quiet persistence even when the weather turns rough.

entries.author: William Wordsworth
entries.original:
I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
entries.reading:
I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
entries.explanation: An initially lonely walk becomes a joyful encounter with daffodils; remembering that scene later brings comfort.

entries.author: William Blake
entries.original:
To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Auguries of Innocence
entries.reading:
To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower
entries.explanation: Small things can invite large questions. This is poetic imagination, rather than a literal scientific claim.

entries.author: 杜甫 · Du Fu
entries.original: 隨風潛入夜，潤物細無聲。
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Spring Night Rain
entries.reading: With the wind it slips into the night, nourishing things softly, without a sound.
entries.explanation: The spring rain helps life without demanding attention. The lines often evoke gentle, unobtrusive care.

entries.author: 王維 · Wang Wei
entries.original: 明月松間照，清泉石上流。
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Autumn Evening in the Mountains
entries.reading: Bright moonlight shines among the pines; a clear spring flows over the stones.
entries.explanation: Light and flowing water form a peaceful mountain scene after rain. Stillness and movement belong together.

entries.author: 王之渙 · Wang Zhihuan
entries.original: 欲窮千里目，更上一層樓。
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Climbing Stork Tower
entries.reading: To see a thousand miles farther, climb another floor.
entries.explanation: A change in vantage point expands the view. The practical image also invites curiosity and continued learning.

entries.author: 蘇軾 · Su Shi
entries.original: 莫聽穿林打葉聲，何妨吟嘯且徐行。
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Calming the Waves
entries.reading: Let the rain sound through the trees; why not sing and walk at an easy pace?
entries.explanation: The speaker meets an unexpected shower with composure. Calmness does not remove difficulty, but changes how it is met.

entries.author: Elias Lönnrot · Finnish oral tradition
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Kalevala — song begins
entries.reading: My mind wishes; my thoughts are stirring.
entries.explanation: The epic opens with the wish to sing. A shared story starts with a person willing to speak and remember.

entries.author: Elias Lönnrot · Finnish oral tradition
entries.original:
Lyökämme käsi kätehen,
sormet sormien lomahan,
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Kalevala — singing together
entries.reading: Let us join hand to hand, fingers interlaced.
entries.explanation: The invitation turns recitation into companionship. The following lines call for sharing good songs.

entries.author: Elias Lönnrot · Finnish oral tradition
entries.original:
Vilu mulle virttä virkkoi,
sae saatteli runoja.
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Kalevala — nature teaches songs
entries.reading: Cold spoke songs to me; rain brought poems.
entries.explanation: Weather becomes a source of language and memory. Inspiration is found in ordinary experience, not only in books.

entries.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Wanderer’s Night Song
entries.reading: Above all the mountain peaks, there is stillness.
entries.explanation: The landscape grows quiet as the poem approaches rest. It invites a pause and also reflects on mortality.

entries.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
entries.original:
Ich ging im Walde
So für mich hin,
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Found
entries.reading: I walked in the woods, quietly on my own.
entries.explanation: An unplanned walk leads to a flower; the poem turns from picking it to caring for its continued growth.

entries.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
entries.original:
Und doch, welch Glück geliebt zu werden!
Und lieben, Götter, welch ein Glück!
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Welcome and Farewell
entries.reading: And yet, what happiness to be loved! And to love—what happiness!
entries.explanation: The ending holds the sadness of parting beside gratitude for love. Joy and sorrow can share one experience.

entries.author: 松尾芭蕉 · Matsuo Bashō
entries.original: 古池や蛙とびこむ水の音
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Old pond
entries.reading: An old pond—a frog jumps in; the sound of water.
entries.explanation: A small sound makes the surrounding stillness noticeable. The poem attends closely to a brief moment.

entries.author: 松尾芭蕉 · Matsuo Bashō
entries.original: あらたふと靑葉若葉の日の光
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Sunlight and new leaves
entries.reading: How wondrous: sunlight on green leaves and new leaves.
entries.explanation: Written in the Nikkō travel passage, the line joins fresh foliage with a feeling of reverence.

entries.author: 松尾芭蕉 · Matsuo Bashō
entries.original: しばらくは瀧に籠るや夏の初
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Behind the waterfall
entries.reading: For a little while, sheltered behind the waterfall: the beginning of summer.
entries.explanation: The travel narrative describes looking out from behind a waterfall. A changed viewpoint refreshes a familiar season.

entries.author: 松尾芭蕉 · Matsuo Bashō
entries.original: 閑さや岩にしみ入るせみの聲
entries.rights: Public-domain original; new prose renderings and explanations.
entries.title: Stillness and cicadas
entries.reading: Stillness—the cicadas’ voices seem to sink into the rocks.
entries.explanation: A sound is used to deepen the impression of stillness. This wording follows the variant recorded with the source text.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A good question can be a small window in a large wall.
entries.explanation: Curiosity makes room for learning before we have an answer.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: Kindness is a language that does not need a perfect accent.
entries.explanation: A patient gesture can make a stranger feel welcome.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: The sky does not ask the lake to hurry its reflection.
entries.explanation: Some understanding arrives when we leave a little quiet.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A shared meal can turn a map into a memory.
entries.explanation: Places become meaningful through the people we meet there.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: The first page is allowed to be imperfect.
entries.explanation: Beginning gives us something real to improve.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: Listening is a way of giving someone room.
entries.explanation: We do not have to fill every pause with our own words.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A flower does not become less beautiful because another flower blooms.
entries.explanation: Appreciating others need not diminish our own worth.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: Rest is also part of a journey.
entries.explanation: A pause can make the next stretch more attentive.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: Noticing one small good thing changes the shape of a day.
entries.explanation: This invites attention to ordinary beauty without denying difficulty.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A library is a room with many doors.
entries.explanation: Each book offers a different way into someone else’s experience.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: The stars can be distant and still make the evening feel close.
entries.explanation: Wonder can connect everyday life with a larger world.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A careful correction is a quiet form of respect.
entries.explanation: Accuracy matters because someone else will rely on the result.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A path becomes familiar one step at a time.
entries.explanation: Practice can be steady and modest rather than spectacular.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A thank-you can travel farther than we know.
entries.explanation: Naming someone’s help lets them know it made a difference.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: The horizon leaves room for another morning.
entries.explanation: A difficult day need not define every day that follows.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: We can disagree and still leave the door open.
entries.explanation: Respect helps a conversation continue after a difference appears.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A seed keeps its own calendar.
entries.explanation: Some growth is happening before it can be seen.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: The best souvenir may be a story told kindly.
entries.explanation: Travel stories can honour people rather than reduce them to stereotypes.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: An honest “I don’t know” is a useful beginning.
entries.explanation: Recognising a gap makes it possible to investigate it.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A small lamp does not have to become the sun to be useful.
entries.explanation: Local help can matter even when it cannot solve everything.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: A little laughter can make space for a deeper breath.
entries.explanation: Gentle humour can welcome people without making someone the target.

entries.title: A small thought
entries.reading: The world is larger than the part we have learned to name.
entries.explanation: There is room to meet unfamiliar languages, ideas and places with curiosity.
